definition: Daniel Jurafsky is a professor of linguistics and computer science at Stanford University, and also an author.
details: Co-created the FrameNet project and authored the definitive textbook for natural language processing. With Daniel Gildea, he is known for developing the first automatic system for semantic role labeling (SRL). He is the author of The Language of Food: A Linguist Reads the Menu (2014) and a textbook on speech and language processing (2000).

explainer.lead: Dan Jurafsky is an American linguist (born 1962). His work spans natural language processing, speech recognition, linguistics and computational linguistics.

contributions.name: The first automatic system for semantic role labeling (SRL, sometimes also referred to as "shallow semantic parsing") was developed by Daniel Gildea and Daniel Jurafsky to automate the FrameNet annotation process in 2002; SRL has since become one of the standard tasks in natural language processing.

timeline.what: Jurafsky received his B.A in linguistics (1983) and Ph.D. in computer science (1992), both at University of California, Berkeley; and then a postdoc at International Computer Science Institute, Berkeley (1992–1995).
Jurafsky was given a MacArthur Fellowship in 2002.
Named Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science
Receives the Atkinson Prize in Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
